facts.title: An orchard of allegory
facts.body: Primavera (c. 1482) gathers Venus, the Graces, Mercury, Flora, Chloris, and Zephyrus in an orange grove. It is one of the most dense mythological programs of the Florentine Renaissance.

facts.title: Venus as quiet ruler
facts.body: Venus stands slightly raised at center, hand raised in a gesture of welcome. Around her the garden becomes a court of love.

facts.title: Mercury clearing the air
facts.body: At far left Mercury lifts his caduceus toward the clouds — often read as clearing winter so spring can enter.

facts.title: The Three Graces dancing
facts.body: Beauty, Joy, and Charm interlace translucent dresses in a circle. Their dance is the painting’s soft metronome.

facts.title: Flora scattering blooms
facts.body: Flora, dressed in blossom, strews flowers forward — spring made person.

facts.title: Chloris becoming Flora
facts.body: Chloris is seized by Zephyrus as flowers spill from her mouth — the metamorphosis that turns nymph into goddess of flowers.

facts.title: Zephyrus lunging in
facts.body: The blue-winged west wind breaks into the grove from the right edge, the only violent motion in an otherwise measured pageant.

facts.title: Cupid above Venus
facts.body: Blindfolded Cupid aims an arrow above Venus — desire that does not look where it strikes.

facts.title: Medici oranges
facts.body: Orange trees (malus medica) may pun on the Medici name. The grove is both paradise and patronage.

facts.title: A botanist’s carpet
facts.body: Hundreds of identifiable flower species carpet the ground — a painted herbal beneath the myth.
